title: CEO Paid a Stranger $100,000 a Month to Marry Her — He Was the Billionaire She Was Trying to Win
description:
One year. $100,000 a month. No touching. No feelings. Divorce on day 366. 💍

Audrey Whitfield runs Whitfield Group, one of the biggest companies in Chicago. But her grandmother has made one thing clear: if Audrey isn't married by Friday, Uncle Martin gets her chair.

So at 30,000 feet, she makes the man in seat 10A an offer. A stranger in a cheap jacket. A "handyman." A box boy from Joliet.

Lucas Ward signs.

Back on the ground, nobody can believe it. His ex, Megan, left him six years ago for a rich man's son, after he paid for every semester of her PhD. Her mother calls him a warehouse boy. Trent Kingsley has security throw him out of the lobby. And the whole company laughs at the CEO who "bought a husband."

Meanwhile, Audrey is chasing the deal of her life: Iron Crest, the biggest fund on earth, run by a founder nobody has ever seen. They call him the Ghost.

On the night of the Crest Gala, in front of 400 guests, the Ghost is finally going to show his face.

And Lucas Ward is on the no-entry list.

⚠️ Disclaimer: This is a fictional story made for entertainment. The characters, voices and scenes in this video were created with AI tools. Any resemblance to real people or events is purely coincidental.

title: He Thought a Toll Booth Worker Was Too Dumb to Notice His Rigged Question. Big Mistake
description:
For thirty years, Dot Kowalski sat in a little glass toll booth on Route 30, counting trucks, reading books and noticing the things everyone else misses. Next month, a camera is taking her job. Tonight, she's on the season finale of America's biggest quiz show, one question away from a million dollars.

Chase Harmon, the slick, smug host of The Final Ladder, thinks she's the perfect punchline. He mocks her job in front of a live studio audience. But Dot spots something he doesn't want anyone to see, and the jokes stop being funny.

Behind the cameras, the producer is panicking. The show can't afford to pay the prize. So during the commercial break, Chase pulls out a secret card, a million-dollar question where every single answer is wrong. Whatever Dot picks, she loses. On live television. Gracefully.

There's just one problem. Thirty years in a toll booth taught Dot exactly how liars behave. They smile too much, and they look away.

And someone in the control room just pressed a button Chase doesn't know about.

Watch to the very end to see what happens when the quietest person in the room turns out to be the smartest, and why the last scene in a little bookstore called Exact Change is the best revenge of all.

If you believe the people who get underestimated are often the ones paying the closest attention, tell us in the comments: what would you do with a million dollars?

Like, subscribe and turn on notifications for more stories where quiet people get the last word.

Hushfall Drama. Quiet people. Loud karma.

This story is fictional. All characters, events and names are made up, and any resemblance to real people or shows is coincidental. This video was created with the help of AI tools, including AI-generated visuals and voices.
